scope: Scoped vocabulary and mathematical definitions. Vocabulary does not create physical instances, causal effects or numerical thresholds.

records.definition: Mutual contributions to a specified joint outcome under declared conditions.
records.finding: A positive coupling coefficient does not prove bounded energy, stability or a necessary edge. Removing a required contribution and losing the target supports the necessity hypothesis; it is not its falsifier.
records.name: Cooperation

records.definition: A restriction on the admissible states, trajectories or operations of a specified model.
records.finding: An inequality is not generally an equality. A constrained optimum needs appropriate feasibility, multiplier and optimality conditions; tightening an inactive constraint need not change the outcome. For differentiable convex objectives/inequalities and affine equalities, the full KKT conditions are sufficient: primal feasibility, nonnegative inequality multipliers, complementary slackness and stationarity. With Slater regularity they are also necessary; arbitrary stationary points of a constrained Lagrangian are not automatically minima.
records.name: Constraint

records.definition: A closed influence path in a specified dynamical or intervention model.
records.finding: Feedback sign and gain magnitude are distinct. Stability needs the actual time domain, dynamics and delay assumptions. det(I-G)=0 is not a universal definition of criticality. For autonomous finite-dimensional linear x[n+1]=M*x[n], asymptotic stability requires all eigenvalues strictly inside the unit circle; boundary cases need additional analysis. For dx/dt=M*x, the corresponding condition is strictly negative real parts.

citations.locator: Chapter 4, Section 4.3, Theorem 4.1, p. 106; author chapter revision 10 August 2012

records.name: Feedback

records.definition: An event or intervention that starts a specified response in an already defined preparation.
records.finding: Deterministic activation and noise-driven escape are different models. A Heaviside term or an uncalibrated Kramers expression does not establish a threshold, persistence or novelty.
records.name: Initiation

records.definition: Production or observation of a specified output under declared conditions.
records.finding: An observable map and an integral of field magnitude do not alone demonstrate localization, persistent objecthood or physical formation.
records.name: Realization

records.definition: A proposed relation from a finer description to a coarser description, relative to an explicit state map.
records.finding: Aggregation by itself does not establish autonomous macro-dynamics or causal consistency. Specify realizable interventions and the map before admitting a causal relation.
records.name: Upward causation

records.definition: A proposed influence of a coarser description on finer dynamics within a compatible intervention model.
records.finding: A macro-variable determined by microstates cannot be varied independently while fixing those same microstates. Avoid counting a re-description as an additional physical cause.
records.name: Downward causation

records.definition: A proposed directed relation between records assigned the same descriptive scale.
records.finding: Equal display levels do not imply symmetric coupling, equal strength or mutual necessity.
records.name: Horizontal causation

records.definition: A proposed feedback configuration connecting descriptions assigned different scales.
records.finding: Cross-level coupling is not identified by a spectral-radius inequality. A stable linear cross-level loop is a counterexample to the proposed threshold.
records.name: Diagonal causation

records.definition: An effective description with an explicitly stated regime of approximate autonomy from omitted variables.
records.finding: Coarse-graining can leave memory and unresolved dependence. A formal path integral is not a demonstrated closure, error bound or valid effective theory.
records.name: Decoupled causation

records.definition: A project rule for evaluating or organizing causal claims.
records.finding: This is a methodological role. Material implication in logic is not by itself physical causation, and a rule does not establish its own empirical applicability.
records.name: Metacausation

records.definition: A time-indexed evolution or operation described in a specified model and observation window.
records.finding: A stationary trajectory is allowed; different initial states need not remain distinguishable. No automatic causal-direction/mode permissions are recovered from the undocumented Causality pairs.
records.name: Process

records.definition: An individuated candidate whose identity and persistence are tested against declared boundaries, perturbations and timescales.
records.finding: Invariance of a set alone does not establish a localized physical object. The Level-0 objecthood gate remains separate from this vocabulary role.
records.name: Object

records.definition: A configuration or regularity identified using a declared representation, comparison rule and scale.
records.finding: Symmetry or correlation can describe a pattern without proving a generative mechanism. The equivalence relation and reference comparison must be explicit.
records.name: Pattern

records.definition: An attribute or observable assigned to an identified bearer or configuration.
records.finding: A property can concern one component. A new symbol or aggregate observable does not establish irreducibility or new physical laws.
records.name: Property

records.definition: A specified outcome; a causal-effect claim additionally requires a contrast and an identification argument.
records.finding: Observation of an output alone is not a causal estimate. Effects need not be persistent, propagate outside a boundary or form new objects.
records.name: Effect

records.definition: A descriptive phase label for distinguishing candidate components or states.
records.finding: The label does not establish minimal building blocks or require a universal developmental sequence.
records.name: Differentiation

records.definition: A descriptive phase label for assembling or coupling previously distinguished components.
records.finding: Integration does not by itself prove stability, necessity of every part or a new level of physical laws.
records.name: Integration

records.definition: A descriptive phase label for organized behavior arising within a specified system and environment.
records.finding: Specify mechanisms and observables. Adaptive feedback is not a universal prerequisite inferred from this label.
records.name: Self-organization

records.definition: A descriptive phase label for a proposed change in organization or effective description.
records.finding: A qualitative change does not prove irreducibility, a universal threshold or successful promotion to a new carrier class.
records.name: Threshold transition

records.definition: A constituent or supporting material role relative to a specified target and system boundary.
records.finding: Identify replaceable classes and feasible interventions; a named substrate is not automatically necessary in every realization.
records.name: Substrate

records.definition: An interface or boundary condition constraining interaction with a specified domain.
records.finding: Distinguish an interface from the enclosed domain. Removing a boundary need not abolish every process; specify permeability and observation time.
records.name: Boundary

records.definition: A configuration used to guide the arrangement or sequence of a specified product or process.
records.finding: Correlation with a product is insufficient to identify templating. A template may also catalyze; these roles need not be exclusive.
records.name: Template

records.definition: A chemical participant that accelerates a reaction while leaving its overall standard Gibbs energy change unchanged.
records.finding: Separate kinetic acceleration from thermodynamic feasibility. Participation and regeneration require a specified reaction; no universal two-site cooperativity threshold is admitted.
records.name: Catalyst

records.definition: A role that adjusts specified system variables or parameters.
records.finding: Regulation can be feed-forward. Feedback requires a closed influence mechanism; overshoot or hysteresis is not uniquely diagnostic.
records.name: Regulation

records.definition: A spatial difference or derivative of a specified potential or other field quantity.
records.finding: A gradient is not a flux. State the quantity, units, transport law and boundary conditions before asserting sustained work or necessity.
records.name: Gradient

records.definition: A bounded or operationally delimited domain for specified contents or processes.
records.finding: Compartments can enhance or hinder an outcome and need not have a membrane. Their effect requires a comparison and a timescale.
records.name: Compartment

records.definition: A role for distinguishable encoded states interpreted through a declared physical realization and decoding convention.
records.finding: Separate token occurrences, symbol types, physical states and information measures. Encoding does not create causation beyond the implementation.
records.name: Information

records.definition: A role for differential persistence or reproduction within a specified ensemble and observation window.
records.finding: Distinguish selection from drift, migration and other frequency-changing processes. An explicit feedback loop is not inferred from the label.
records.name: Selection

records.definition: An input available for consumption or use by a specified process.
records.finding: Stock, concentration, energy and supply rate are different quantities. Resource and substrate roles may overlap and need an explicit balance model.
records.name: Resource

records.definition: A restriction on a specified set of allowable configurations or transitions.
records.finding: A restriction can be inactive or make a problem infeasible. It does not guarantee entropy reduction, stability or a conservation law.
records.name: Constraint

records.definition: A mechanism that transfers specified matter, charge, energy or encoded signals across a defined separation.
records.finding: Colocation or connectivity is not measured transport. Identify flux, timescale and mechanism before asserting necessity.
records.name: Transport

records.definition: The surroundings relative to an explicitly chosen system boundary.
records.finding: External to the boundary does not mean statistically exogenous or causally unconfounded. Bidirectional coupling may remain.
records.name: Environment

records.definition: A project family of field excitations and modes whose identity depends on a specified field model.
records.finding: Mode count, excitation number, amplitude and energy are distinct. Allowed levels and typical critical counts are historical heuristics.
records.name: Field / mode carriers

records.definition: A project family of material bodies individuated by declared operational boundaries.
records.finding: One body is possible; pair and triad requirements belong to particular mechanisms, not to the carrier family.
records.name: Physical body carriers

records.definition: A project family of material units such as atoms, molecules, bonds, complexes and cells.
records.finding: These units are not interchangeable counts. Concentration or amount needs a stated conversion model before any particle-count interpretation.
records.name: Functional material carriers

records.definition: A project family of structural features such as edges, paths and loops in a declared representation.
records.finding: Edge count, loop count, cycle length and participating vertex count differ. Topology does not alone identify an active physical feedback process.
records.name: Topological / configurational carriers

records.definition: A project family of encoded or represented states and symbols.
records.finding: Specify occurrence versus type and the state partition. Counts, capacity and information measures have different semantics even when dimensionless.
records.name: Informational / symbolic carriers

records.definition: A project family of agents and populations relative to a membership rule and time window.
records.finding: Members, roles and events are different units. An agency label is a modeling choice, not a universal carrier threshold.
records.name: Agent / population carriers

records.definition: One material body under a declared operational boundary and identity rule.
records.finding: The existence of one body does not require two or three participants; those numbers would describe a separate target motif.
records.name: Physical body

records.definition: One field-excitation instance under a specified field model and detection convention.
records.finding: Excitation number is different from number of modes, energy and amplitude; no universal minimum of two is admitted.
records.name: Field excitation

records.definition: One mode identified by a specified decomposition and equivalence convention.
records.finding: A single mode and a three-mode interaction are different counting questions. A triad threshold cannot define every mode.
records.name: Resonant mode

records.definition: One atom instance under a stated sample and individuation convention.
records.finding: Chemical identity labels a type, not an individual atom. The historical minimum of two is not a universal atom count.
records.name: Atom

records.definition: One molecule instance of a specified species in a defined sample.
records.finding: Species identity and instance identity differ. Concentration, occupancy and molecule count require separate units and context.
records.name: Molecule

records.definition: One specified bond instance between identified participants.
records.finding: Count bonds separately from atoms and interacting pairs; multiplicity and representation rules must be explicit.
records.name: Bond instance

records.definition: One specified catalytic or binding site in an identified material structure.
records.finding: Site number is different from site occupancy, turnover and cooperativity. No universal critical site count of two is supported.
records.name: Active site

records.definition: One macromolecular assembly instance under stated composition and boundary criteria.
records.finding: Assembly count does not specify subunit count, stoichiometry, stability or successful functional formation.
records.name: Macromolecular complex

records.definition: One cell instance in a defined sample under a stated boundary and identification procedure.
records.finding: Counting a cell does not establish complete autonomy. Population thresholds are separate claims with target-specific evidence.
records.name: Cell

records.definition: One directed or undirected relation instance in a specified graph representation.
records.finding: State graph type, direction, relation type and treatment of parallel edges. The count alone does not establish physical interaction.
records.name: Interaction edge

records.definition: One closed path under a specified cycle-equivalence and activity convention.
records.finding: One loop can contain several participants. Graph cycles, independent cycle-space dimension and active feedback loops are different quantities.
records.name: Feedback loop

records.definition: One token occurrence under a specified alphabet, segmentation and representation.
records.finding: A token occurrence is not a distinct symbol type or distinguishable system state. Capacity thresholds require a separate model.
records.name: Information token

records.definition: One participant satisfying a declared agency and membership rule in an observation window.
records.finding: An agent can be counted alone. Collective coordination thresholds cannot be imported as the minimum definition of an agent.
records.name: Agent

records.definition: One neural state or activity pattern under an explicit spatial, temporal and state-partition convention.
records.finding: Continuous activity has no unique discrete state count without a partition. Representation capacity is not a universal neural threshold.
records.name: Neural state / activity pattern

records.definition: A historical display group for the author's proposed prephysical foundation.
records.finding: A hypothesis vocabulary, not an established physical stage; the conditional Level-0 rules and unsuccessful objecthood case state the actual evidence boundary.
records.name: Proto Field

records.definition: A historical display group for quantum descriptions and examples.
records.finding: Display placement is not a unique scale, a temporal stage or proof that quantum systems arise from the proposed foundation.
records.name: Quantum

records.definition: A historical display group for atomic and related material examples.
records.finding: Domains overlap; the number 2 does not establish derivation depth or a universal transition from every quantum description.
records.name: Atomic

records.definition: A historical display group for biochemical examples.
records.finding: Biochemical organization requires mechanism-specific review, not inference from its position after atoms.
records.name: Biochemical

records.definition: A historical display group for cellular examples.
records.finding: A cellular display group does not establish autonomous objecthood or a universal four-phase construction rule.
records.name: Cellular

records.definition: A historical display group for multicellular structures and functions.
records.finding: Functions, organs, regulation and organism formation require separate relations; grouping them does not make their carriers interchangeable.
records.name: Multicellular

records.definition: A historical display group for behavior and cognition examples.
records.finding: Behavioral description does not prove a new physical law or a unique complexity rank.
records.name: Behavioral

records.definition: A historical display group for social organization examples.
records.finding: Social group placement does not identify a formation mechanism, minimal population or distinct physical stratum.
records.name: Social

records.definition: A dictionary-only proposal for technological examples.
records.finding: No level-8 source catalogue exists. Technology overlaps several domains; no nodes or transition are admitted by this label.
records.name: Technological

records.definition: A dictionary-only proposal for planetary examples.
records.finding: No level-9 source catalogue exists. Planetary scale does not imply greater complexity or later origin than society.
records.name: Planetary

records.definition: A dictionary-only proposal for civilizational examples.
records.finding: No level-10 source catalogue exists. This rubric overlaps social and technological descriptions and is not a validated physical layer.
records.name: Civilizational

records.definition: A dictionary-only proposal for spacefaring infrastructure examples.
records.finding: No level-11 source catalogue exists. Specified engineering systems would need their own evidence and admission decisions.
records.name: Spacefaring infrastructure

records.definition: A dictionary-only proposal for cosmic examples.
records.finding: No level-12 source catalogue exists. Cosmic chronology cannot be inferred from placement after society or infrastructure; mechanism narratives remain unreviewed.
records.name: Cosmic

records.definition: A dictionary-only speculative placeholder.
records.finding: No level-13 source catalogue exists and no established target domain, mechanism or empirical admission is asserted.
records.name: Upper speculative
